globeDisc.note: only pixels inside this circle are analysed

frameSelection.source: orbit video, 4K, 1176 frames (frame number = position in the video, 1-based)
frameSelection.timeRule: hourly: frame n is 2020-01-19T13:00 + (n - 112) hours; checked against the date stamp printed on all 12 frames; time zone not stated
frameSelection.note: random frames, not evenly spaced in time; `order` is time order

regionMethod: The globe rotates, so the camera centre (lon/lat) of every frame was ESTIMATED by matching an orthographic projection of a flat world map to the frame (scripts/fit_camera.py, error about a few degrees; coastlines checked on all 12 frames). Each disc pixel is converted to lon/lat and given a region from lon/lat boxes (scripts/regions.py, first matching region wins, boxes include nearby sea). Region numbers describe only the VISIBLE part of the region: `visibleFraction` = share of the region's area facing the camera, `reliable` = visibleFraction >= 0.5. Pixels near the globe edge are squashed and count the same as centre pixels. Strips run west to east in longitude across the region's box (48 strips); a strip with no visible pixels is null.
